metadata.title: Legislator Says Multiple Fatalities in Squamish, B.C., Flood Zone

sources.news_title: RCMP say third body found in Squamish, B.C., boat tragedy
sources.text:
SQUAMISH — The waters of the Squamish River roared under rainy skies Friday, as search and rescue crews recovered the bodies of three people who died when a boat overturned in the swollen waterway north of Vancouver, following days of heavy rain and flooding in the region.
Insp. Robert Dykstra, the officer in charge of the Sea to Sky RCMP, said there were originally about eight people aboard the boat Thursday, and police said no one is unaccounted for.
But Dykstra wasn't sure why they were on the water or what caused the boat to overturn.
"I do believe that they ran into something. That's all I really know at this point," he told reporters on Friday.
Dykstra said he believed the boat was local to Squamish and he wasn't aware of any injuries among the survivors of the incident.
The tragedy came after southwest British Columbia was drenched by a series of storms that brought more than 300 millimetres of rain to some areas this week.
The Sea to Sky corridor, including Squamish and Pemberton, was among the areas hardest hit.
Dykstra said police got the call at around 1:50 p.m. on Thursday but it took time for responders to gain access to the area because of a road washout and the state of the raging river.
Police initially said two people had died and a third was missing, but a third body was recovered by Friday afternoon.
Three full white body bags were unloaded from a helicopter at the airport in Squamish around 1:30 p.m., as low-lying clouds rolled in.
Police have not released any details about the victims or survivors.
Dykstra called the situation "tragic."
"You never know exactly why people are doing what they're doing sometimes," he said, adding that "there could be any number of reasons" for the boat being on the water.
Dykstra said the best thing for people to do during major weather events is stay home and stay safe, especially around rapidly moving waters.
"These waters are unforgiving when they're going fast."
All of the rainfall warnings that had blanketed the region over the past week were lifted by Friday, but as weather conditions eased, effects of the deluge were still being felt.
The entire village of Pemberton, about 90 kilometres north of Squamish, remained under an evacuation alert. Evacuation orders imposed by the nearby Lil'wat First Nation, and in Zeballos on Vancouver Island, also remained in place, although an order for parts of Pemberton was downgraded to alert status.
A shelter-in-place advisory issued Thursday for some residents about 16 kilometres north of Squamish was lifted Friday. Still, residents were advised not to drive across flooded roads, and RCMP told residents to stay out of flood zones.
BC Emergency Health Services said it received a call at 2:48 p.m. on Thursday about the boat incident near the 15900 block of Squamish Valley Road. No one was taken to hospital, it said.
At the Squamish airport earlier Friday, a white pickup truck pulled an RCMP boat into the parking lot as members of the local search and rescue team gathered inside their headquarters before deploying to recover the third victim.
Legislator Jeremy Valeriote, who represents West Vancouver-Sea to Sky, said he was "devastated" and his thoughts were with the victims' families.
Valeriote, who was re-elected as the riding's Green legislator last month, said the Sea to Sky region "is a strong and resilient community."
"But no one should have to navigate this alone."
Valeriote said he and his team would support people however they could as the community begins recovering.
At an unrelated event on Friday, B.C. premier-designate Lorne Doerkson called the situation "very serious" and said he intended to visit the area.
"It's pretty serious in our province right now. So (my) heart goes out to those families that are dealing with the losses. Of course the communities as well. These are small communities and everybody is going to feel the pain in those communities," he said.
Wilson Williams, chairperson of the Squamish Nation, said at the same event that he was "calling upon Mother Nature" to protect those in areas dealing with the hazardous weather.
The province's River Forecast Centre downgraded warnings it had issued for the south coast to a lower-level high streamflow advisory. It also ended flood watches for Fraser Valley north, the central coast and east Vancouver Island.
Meanwhile, residents of coastal areas of southwest B.C. were facing a new flooding risk, even as rains eased, with warnings of a storm surge that could raise sea levels.
Environment Canada said the surge could hit low-lying and exposed coastal areas of Metro Vancouver, southeast Vancouver Island and the southern Gulf Islands.
It said elevated water levels surpassing tidal predictions were being driven by high winds and "enhanced wave activity," and could last into the weekend.
This report by The Canadian Press was first published Nov. 13, 2026.
Brenna Owen, The Canadian Press

sources.news_title: 3 dead after boat crash near Squamish
RCMP Say 3 Dead After Floodwaters Hit BC
sources.text:
Three people are dead following a boating incident in the Squamish Valley north of Vancouver, where days of heavy rain have caused widespread flooding, RCMP say.
Squamish RCMP initially reported on Nov. 13 that two people had died and a third was missing, while all other individuals involved had been accounted for.
In a later update on Nov. 13, police confirmed that searchers had located the third person, leaving no one unaccounted for. The incident occurred on Nov. 12 at approximately 1:52 p.m.
The response involved Squamish Search and Rescue, RCMP Air Services, the Lower Mainland District Integrated Emergency Response Team, the RCMP Underwater Recovery Team and West Coast Marine Services.
Flooding has also forced residents of Paradise Valley, about 16 kilometres north of Squamish, to shelter in place after after drenching storms triggered flooding following more than 300 millimetres of rain in areas of southwest B.C. this week.
The Village of Pemberton has issued an evacuation order for properties along Airport Road, while the rest of the village remains under an evacuation alert and shelter-in-place advisory. The Lil'wat First Nation and the Village of Zeballos have also issued evacuation orders for affected properties.
B.C. MLA Jeremy Valeriote, who represents West Vancouver-Sea to Sky, said on social media he was “devastated” by the incident and that his thoughts were with the families of the victims. He also acknowledged the difficult conditions facing residents, businesses and first responders.
Valeriote said the Sea to Sky region “is a strong and resilient community, but no one should have to navigate this alone.” He added that his team would support residents as the community began its recovery.
Environment Canada said a series of intense storms had brought significant rainfall and strong winds to coastal and interior British Columbia since Nov. 10, raising concerns about flooding in several communities.
In a Nov. 12 weather summary, the agency reported that Port Mellon had received 307 millimetres of rain, followed by Kennedy Lake with 263 millimetres, Porteau Cove with 140 millimetres, Whistler-Callaghan Valley with 139 millimetres, Port Alberni Airport with 137 millimetres, and Squamish Airport with 135 millimetres.
Environment Canada also issued a coastal flooding statement early Nov. 13, warning that storm surges, high tides, and strong winds could flood low-lying areas of Metro Vancouver, particularly around Boundary Bay and Semiahmoo Bay. Winds could gust between 60 and 80 kilometres per hour, with the risk of coastal flooding extending into the weekend.
Meanwhile, the Squamish-Lillooet Regional District said the B.C. River Forecast Centre had issued a flood warning for the Pemberton Valley, Howe Sound, and Sea-to-Sky corridor. The warning reflected concerns about rising river levels following several days of heavy rainfall, with communities in the affected areas facing potential flooding.
Most of the rainfall warnings that had blanketed the region were lifted Nov. 12, although yellow warnings remained in place for western, northern and inland Vancouver Island.
The warnings forecast heavy rain into late in the afternoon on Nov. 13, with the highest rainfall expected near Zeballos and Tahsis in northwest Vancouver Island.

sources.news_title: 2 dead, 1 missing after boating incident in Squamish area following flooding
sources.text:
2 dead, 1 missing after boating incident in Squamish area following flooding
|                            Getting your Trinity Audio player ready...                        | 
Two people are dead and one person is missing after a boating incident in the Squamish Valley Thursday (Nov. 12).
Squamish RCMP responded to the boat incident that involved multiple people around 1:52 p.m. on Thursday. Two people have since been confirmed dead and another is unaccounted for.
Police say all other people have been accounted for.
RCMP said that due to water levels and challenging weather conditions, search and rescue and recovery efforts were “extremely difficult and unsafe” for emergency responders on Thursday. The search is resuming Friday.
“The weather and river conditions have played a significant role in the response efforts,” Squamish RCMP Cpl. Ashley MacKay said.
“Weather patterns, water levels, and river conditions can change rapidly, and those factors are being continuously assessed as search and recovery efforts continue. We are asking the public to stay off the water at this time due to dangerous flow rates and debris throughout the river systems.”
North Shore Rescue posted to social media Friday that it responded Thursday to a mutual aid request from Squamish Search and Rescue, adding that it is back up in Squamish Friday with swiftwater and hoist crews.
West Vancouver-Sea to Sky MLA-elect Jeremy Valeriote issued a statement Friday following the reports of fatalities in the region after the flooding.
“I’m devastated to hear of the deaths in Squamish, and my thoughts are with their families and loved ones during this incredibly difficult time,” he said.
Valeriote said that for the past week, the region has been “grappling with the impacts of severe flooding, responding to warnings, evacuations, and significant disruption.” He added it has been an incredibly difficult and exhausting time for residents, businesses and first responders.
“This news brings another layer of heartbreak to a community that has already been through so much.”
